title: Filler-Token Substitution: Is the CoT Computation or Theater?

original_idea.body:
# Filler-Token Substitution: Is the CoT Computation or Theater?

**Problem:** Causal chain: CoT improves accuracy -> we assume the improvement comes from the legible reasoning -> we trust the CoT as a window into computation. Under-studied link for a given model/task: replacing CoT content with meaningless filler tokens of equal length tests whether the gain is from extra compute (theater) vs. the actual reasoning (faithful).

**Direction:** On arithmetic, multi-hop QA, and logic tasks, compare three conditions for a small open reasoning model: (a) real CoT, (b) equal-length filler ('...' / random tokens), (c) no CoT. Measure accuracy across task types. The faithful signature is: real CoT >> filler >= no-CoT. The 'theater' signature is: filler approx real CoT. Success: a task-by-task faithfulness map.

**Why it matters:** Tells us for which task families CoT is a genuine causal record (safe to monitor) vs. mere compute padding (unsafe to trust). A concrete, train-free contribution to the 'is CoT faithful?' open problem, runnable on one GPU.

**Relevant context:** Lanham et al. (arXiv 2307.13702) introduced filler-token interventions and found CoT gains are not pure test-time compute on some tasks; later work shows larger models produce less faithful reasoning. A clean per-task-family replication on open models is feasible and useful.
